COVID PPE Spending Spree: R80-million in 15 days

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How the city of JHB busted the Covid emergency regulations. Who got what and how much did you the already distressed ratepayer fork out?

Unique Selling Point:
We have the draft report with all the information already. Can go to some of the companies - better on TV than in print.

Summary:
For two days last week 270 Johannesburg City council members battled out issues at Gallagher estate and achieved just about -nothing. The meals alone cost ratepayers R250 000 per day.

“Why couldn’t they just do it on Zoom like everyone else” asked a council member? Or rather why couldn’t they use the R400 million rand council chamber built specially for the purpose of holding council meetings?

But those questions are for another day, because the real reason the meeting fell apart is because of a draft audit report prepared by the City’s auditors on eighty million rand spent on Covid procurement for the city in just 15 days.

HAVE WE NOT LEARNT THAT EMERGENCY PROCUREMENT IS A LICENCE TO LOOT?

From the 16th March 2020, before lockdown even began, to the end of March 2020. So even as residents rates have shot up, and many have lost their jobs and can’t pay – an excel spreadsheet of covid-preneurs have made a killing.



Further information:
RISING RATES ABOVE INFLATION
And its not just ratepayers that are concerned about skyrocketing rates and taxes, as the council members were sitting down to their three course lunch at Gallagher estate, the Reserve Bank governor Lesetja Kanyago was warning that municipal rates and taxes are increasing above inflation. Just to add substance to these figures he gave examples. Water tariffs have risen by 213% since 2010, electricity by 177% and rates and taxes by 118 %.

ITS ONLY MILLIONS NOT THE USUAL BILLIONS

South Africans are so used to massive numbers that if its not billions we hardly even notice. But we should notice because the city is not running a clean administration and we have all the figures to prove it. And yes those figures do amount to billions. But for now lets look at some of the specifics in the draft report that the mayor Geoff Makhubu refused to table at council – which is when the meeting disintegrated.

The report details the amounts for deep cleaning, hand sanitizer, masks, gloves and disinfectant. Each company is listed and what we paid for each item. So we know that we bought 1000 buckets and some wet wipes which cost us R867 per bucket. According to the auditors we paid R742 thousand rand too much to E and B interiors. And so it goes. We know that Westinghouse Brake and equipment charged us close to R500 per 1litre bottle of hand sanitizer – R364 thousand rand more than what we should have paid. And on and on it goes down the spread sheet.

The JPC or Johannesburg Property company spent millions deep cleaning buildings – but no one was there. The libraries, for example are still not open. And these are just a few of the figures we know about – according to the report the auditors could not perform proper audits because most of the expenditure, around R50million rands of it, was incurred with no supporting documentation.

The report is also clear that the accounting officer should ensure disciplinary steps are taken against officials who flouted the supply chain regulations, treasury’s circular, and the regulations of the disaster management act.

Both the leader of the DA in the city – Leah Knott and the leader of the EFF Chair Councillor Novela will be interviewed. We will ask for interviews from the audit team and the city manager and the mayor. We will need Tony’s track and trace skills to find out who are the directors and shareholders of companies that really ripped this thing and then we will go and see some of them. Companies for example like Pimp my computer cat, communications companies etc. We have the evidence we just need the go ahead. Can shoot as soon as that comes through.

And just to make things interesting – we will try and find out about the other R600 million spent on Covid supplies after March!





Extra Budget Items:
May need extra day to go and doorstop some of the companies -depends on how far we want to take it

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT SICK CITY TX SUNDAY 01st NOVEMBER 2020

Commentary One
As lockdown loomed, corrupt officials and suppliers across the country jumped on to the Covid19 money bus. Eight months later the SIU told Parliament they are investigating R10. 5 billion in PPE corruption. THAT’S TEN POINT FIVE BILLION RAND.

President Ramaphosa
The PPE scandal as you said, the WHO has said it is murder and I do take that view as well, those who have hiked prices, and in some cases by 800%

Commentary Two
In Gauteng alone, R2.2 billion rand of Covid graft is under investigation, so by comparison Johannesburg’s very own PPE scandal is small potatoes, but not for ratepayers and councilors who were blocked from getting answers.

Leah Knott in Council
Please instead of us getting 50 different reports that detail everything and nothing of what is going on in the city, can we get a detailed report of what is being procured for Covid. Why, where did it go, and how much did it cost?!

Commentary Three
Leah Knott is the Johannesburg DA caucus leader. For weeks the DA, the EFF and other councilors have been screaming for information, and trying to piece together corruption from leaked documents

Leah Knott in council
The following amounts have to be justified- surgical masks R800 000, sanitizer and masks again R630 000 and most importantly the R16 million rand we mentioned for the sanitizing of various offices

Commentary Four
In September a draft internal audit was leaked. It revealed that Johannesburg and it’s entities like City Power, Pikitup, Johannesburg water, and Metrobus to name a few, had grossly overspent on PPE and blown R80 million rand in just 15 days in March.

Leah Knott
it’s been a bumpy ride and we have had several collapses of council because these audits have not been brought

Commentary Four A
EFF Regional secretary Silumko Mabona

Silumko Mabona
The issue was that we don't have an audited detailed report of how much the city spent in terms of Covid19 and as political parties we felt this is important in terms of holding the executive accountable

Commentary Five
While the councilors remained in the dark, Carte Blanche had a copy of that draft audit and began phoning suppliers to check if they had ripped off ratepayers

Masa to supplier
What does Channel connect do? Is this what you do for a business, do you specialize in PPE?

Anele from Channel Connect
Channel connect is a trading company. I am focusing strictly on logistics and then we saw an opportunity because the masks were in demand.

Commentary Six
Joburg water bought R3.3 million rand’s worth of masks from this company

Anele
I was supplied for R27 00 rand and I charged R33,00 I had five rand extra for me

Commentary Seven
But that R5.00 on 100 000 masks translates to R500 000 mark up on an already overpriced product.

Anele
Mamela -when you are selling something, it’s up to somebody to buy it or leave it.

Commentary eight
And buy them they did- city entities gobbled up overpriced PPE. It didn’t matter if your business was carpets, construction or brakes and clutches- there was money to be made!

LINK
According to this report a communications company was also a supplier to the city, now they charged the city R339.25 for a 500 ml bottle of hand sanitizer. Here we are able to pick up a bottle for R59.90

Leah
We have a company that deals in IT technology for example that supplying sanitizing of buildings and hand sanitizer – but they are currently being prosecuted in the courts at the moment for defrauding the city of computers that were never delivered

Commentary nine
But it wasn’t just a mask, glove and sanitizer frenzy- from City power to Joburg water and beyond to the market, it was spray time!

Music sequence spraying montage

Leah Knott
JPC spent R16 million rand on the first two weeks of lockdown on fogging buildings.

Commentary ten
In level 5, libraries were closed and no one could go to the Joburg theatre, but that didn’t stop the Johannesburg property company or JPC, dishing out purchase orders to deep clean city buildings

Leah Knott
There is no reason to fog those buildings when no one is there, and in other cases what was the benefit of that huge expense instead of proper protocols which every business in the country has implemented safely. Nobody is fogging buildings every second day.

Commentary eleven
Access was severely restricted at the Metro Building when it was deep cleaned, but now that councilors are bustling through the corridors, our undercover footage reveals there is no sanitizer at any of the lifts on the floors we visited, and some of the dispensers don’t work.

Pushing dispenser

Commentary twelve
At the main entrance, where sanitizer could have cost more than a bottle of whisky, that point is not lost on chairperson of the municipal public accounts committee, Thandi Nontenja, who uses this staff entrance underground.

Thandi
If you go through this building this way there is one sanitizer it has not been working for three weeks. How many employees of the city besides the 270 councilors who presses the lift. On all the floors there is no sanitizer but the city has spent millions on PPE

Commentary thirteen
Nontenja’s committee also tried to get details of the graft. Their role is oversight and governance, but her committee was never even given the draft audit report

Masa
Who is ultimately responsible?
Thandi
The person where the buck stops is the city manager, because all manager’s report to him. He should give us the information

LINK
We have done everything we can to try and get answers from the mayor and the municipal manager, but the impression we are getting is that they are ducking and diving




Commentary fourteen
In their response to Carte Blanche they said they could not answer questions before the final audit was tabled at council- but that only happened on Tuesday – five months after the audit was completed! Councilors had run out of patience with Mayor Geoff Makhubo.

Councilor Shakira Choonara
Please just have respect. A detailed report consists of unit prices, consists of proper information not this wishy washy report that he has given us
Speaker
That is not a point of order!
Councilor
No it’s a point of order!

Commentary Fifteen
Eventually the mayor came to the point.

Mayor Geoff Makhubo
If you look at the next reports on what was bought, from who by which department, from the figures we have up to the 14th October R240 million was actually spent by the city- on what, the report will come

Commentary Sixteen
So this week the audit of the 15 day spending spree in March was released, but we are still waiting for details on how the city spent the additional R240 million

Leah
These reports that we tabled now were uploaded over the weekend, and eventually I said to our chief whip this is like they have given us a haystack and now we are trying to find the needle

Commentary Seventeen
Whereas the draft report found gross contravention of applicable laws and regulations, the final report is less damning, and finds that some of the procurement did not follow a fair, transparent, equitable, competitive and cost effective process- contravened applicable laws, and the Constitution of South Africa. The man who must account is the city manager – and the mayor made it HIS problem on Tuesday.

Mayor Geoff Makhubo
The city manager must deploy senior officials who are going to be answering the questions wena from JDA what did you spend on, and why?

Commentary eighteen
Questionable Emergency PPE spend in those 15 frenzied days in March totals R66 million, of which R16 million, paid to only four companies for all that deep cleaning, is being investigated by the S.I.U.


Geoff Makhubo
JPC remains a problem. And if you see the transgressions JPC comes up over and over again.

Commentary nineteen
But what about the other PPE? Did we get fair value when we spent R3.4 million on digital thermometers from a construction company? Or did we pay R389 for a box of 6 bars of lifebuoy soap from a company with an untraceable Durban address, owned by a 22 year old and her foreign partner.

Thandi Nontenja Municipal Public Accounts committee chair
Who are these people? And how are they related to one another? And what made us to go to KZN? There are so many questions and there are so few answers.

Commentary twenty
The city’s finances are precarious, our rates and taxes have rocketed above inflation.
What is needed says Thandi Nontenja is a disciplinary board where real consequences can be meted out to corrupt officials.

Thandi
Ok the problem we have in this city is there is a lack of consequence management
Masa
It seems these entities were able to procure with no accountability
Yes.
There is no disciplinary here. They get away with murder

THE END 10 02


PROMO ONE
After months of delays the City of Johannesburg finally released an audit detailing how they had spent emergency PPE funds in March. Did the residents get value for money.

PROMO TWO
The city of Johannesburg spent over R16 million rand defogging city buildings deep in lockdown. Lifesaver or waste of ratepayers money. The SIU is investigating.

PROMO THREE
It didn’t matter if you were a carpet company or sold breaks and clutches- as lockdown loomed, everyone climbed in to sell emergency PPE to the city of Johannesburg.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): How the city of JHB busted the Covid emergency regulations. Who got what and how much did you the already distressed ratepayer fork out?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have the draft report with all the information already. Can go to some of the companies - better on TV than in print.
metadata.Summary: For two days last week 270 Johannesburg City council members battled out issues at Gallagher estate and achieved just about -nothing. The meals alone cost ratepayers R250 000 per day. “Why couldn’t they just do it on Zoom like everyone else” asked a council member? Or rather why couldn’t they use the R400 million rand council chamber built specially for the purpose of holding council meetings? But those questions are for another day, because the real reason the meeting fell apart is because of a draft audit report prepared by the City’s auditors on eighty million rand spent on Covid procurement for the city in just 15 days. HAVE WE NOT LEARNT THAT EMERGENCY PROCUREMENT IS A LICENCE TO LOOT? From the 16th March 2020, before lockdown even began, to the end of March 2020. So even as residents rates have shot up, and many have lost their jobs and can’t pay – an excel spreadsheet of covid-preneurs have made a killing.
metadata.Further information: RISING RATES ABOVE INFLATION And its not just ratepayers that are concerned about skyrocketing rates and taxes, as the council members were sitting down to their three course lunch at Gallagher estate, the Reserve Bank governor Lesetja Kanyago was warning that municipal rates and taxes are increasing above inflation. Just to add substance to these figures he gave examples. Water tariffs have risen by 213% since 2010, electricity by 177% and rates and taxes by 118 %. ITS ONLY MILLIONS NOT THE USUAL BILLIONS South Africans are so used to massive numbers that if its not billions we hardly even notice. But we should notice because the city is not running a clean administration and we have all the figures to prove it. And yes those figures do amount to billions. But for now lets look at some of the specifics in the draft report that the mayor Geoff Makhubu refused to table at council – which is when the meeting disintegrated. The report details the amounts for deep cleaning, hand sanitizer, masks, gloves and disinfectant. Each company is listed and what we paid for each item. So we know that we bought 1000 buckets and some wet wipes which cost us R867 per bucket. According to the auditors we paid R742 thousand rand too much to E and B interiors. And so it goes. We know that Westinghouse Brake and equipment charged us close to R500 per 1litre bottle of hand sanitizer – R364 thousand rand more than what we should have paid. And on and on it goes down the spread sheet. The JPC or Johannesburg Property company spent millions deep cleaning buildings – but no one was there. The libraries, for example are still not open. And these are just a few of the figures we know about – according to the report the auditors could not perform proper audits because most of the expenditure, around R50million rands of it, was incurred with no supporting documentation. The report is also clear that the accounting officer should ensure disciplinary steps are taken against officials who flouted the supply chain regulations, treasury’s circular, and the regulations of the disaster management act. Both the leader of the DA in the city – Leah Knott and the leader of the EFF Chair Councillor Novela will be interviewed. We will ask for interviews from the audit team and the city manager and the mayor. We will need Tony’s track and trace skills to find out who are the directors and shareholders of companies that really ripped this thing and then we will go and see some of them. Companies for example like Pimp my computer cat, communications companies etc. We have the evidence we just need the go ahead. Can shoot as soon as that comes through. And just to make things interesting – we will try and find out about the other R600 million spent on Covid supplies after March!
